title: Long Pressed Name
spaceBreakdown:
- int i, j, n, m: four scalars → O(1)
- no containers, no recursion, no heap allocation
- not counted: input strings name, typed
approach: Use two pointers: `i` walks through `name`, `j` walks through `typed`. At each step, if `name[i] == typed[j]`, advance both (a genuine match). Otherwise, `typed[j]` must be a long press - i.e., equal to `typed[j-1]` - in which case we advance only `j`. If neither condition holds, return false. After consuming all of `typed`, every character of `name` must have been matched (`i == name.length`). This is correct because long presses only add consecutive duplicates, so the character sequence of `typed` must be `name`'s sequence with some runs extended.
hints: When scanning both strings left to right, what must be true about a character in `typed` that doesn't match the current character in `name`? Each character in `name` appears at least once in `typed`, in the same order.

Two pointers: `i` into `name`, `j` into `typed`. For `name="alex"`, `typed="aaleex"`: `name[0]='a'` matches `typed[0]='a'` (advance both), then `typed[1]='a'` doesn't match `name[1]='l'` but equals `typed[0]`, so it's a long press (advance `j` only).

**Name longer than typed in a group** - typed doesn't have enough copies of a character
`Input: name = "aa", typed = "a"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: returning `true` at loop exit without checking `i == n` → returns true

**Long press on last character** - typed has trailing repeats after name is fully consumed
`Input: name = "ab", typed = "abbb"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: using `while (i < n && j < m)` and returning `j == m` → returns false (j=2, m=4)

**First character mismatch** - typed's first character differs from name's
`Input: name = "b", typed = "ab"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking `typed[j] == typed[j-1]` without a `j > 0` guard → accesses typed[-1], undefined behavior

**Extra different character at end** - typed ends with a character not in name
`Input: name = "abc", typed = "abcd"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: using `while (i < n && j < m)` as loop condition → exits when i=3, j=3, returns `i == n` = true

followUps.q: If `typed` can also contain at most k inserted typo characters (not long presses), how do you adapt?
followUps.a: Add a skip budget k. When `typed[j]` matches neither `name[i]` nor `typed[j-1]`, decrement k and advance j only. Return false if k drops below 0. O(n + m) time, O(1) space.

followUps.q: If name and typed are each up to 10^9 characters but given as run-length encoded lists of (char, count) pairs, how do you solve it?
followUps.a: Walk both group lists with two pointers. For each name group (c, cnt), the corresponding typed group must have the same character c and count >= cnt; advance the typed pointer past that group. O(g1 + g2) time where g1, g2 are group counts, O(1) space.

followUps.q: If `typed` arrives as a one-character-at-a-time stream and cannot be stored, can you still decide?
followUps.a: Yes. Keep index i into name and the last received character. For each incoming c: if i < n and name[i] == c, advance i; else if c equals the last character, it's a long press; else return false. After the stream ends, return i == n. O(n) space for name, O(1) additional.
